name: gene-hooks
description: Hooks for every Claude Code session of Gene's: a bootstrap loader (hooks/boot.sh) that runs each hook from the newest installed version, the Pacific clock on every prompt and tool result (on a Skill call's result, since 1.20.0, SMADPickleBot #1169, a pointer to the newest installed copy of the skill when the session loaded an older one, so a long-running session never follows a stale skill; and on the clock's prompt branch, since 1.16.0, the model check, SMADPickleBot #423: once an hour per box, builtins only, the prompted desktop session is told to read the weekly Fable window with get_usage and set every desktop session to the newest Opus at 99% or back to the newest Fable after the reset, its own by a peer, a session on another machine by message (1.18.0), and since 1.17.0 to start the account handover once at 99% of the all-models window; since 1.19.0, SMADPickleBot #1144, once every session is on Opus the check holds until the Fable window's weekly reset, recorded by hooks/model-check-hold.sh, reading only the all-models window meanwhile; since 1.24.0, SMADPickleBot #1475, the switch to Opus comes at 95%, or sooner when the rise since the last reading, carried forward an hour, reaches 99%, each check noting its reading with model-check-hold.sh note, and a check two intervals overdue says it ran late; since 1.25.0, SMADPickleBot #1491, the due check reads the desktop app's own record of each session's model with hooks/model-check-records.py, hands it to the session to switch every session recorded off the target, breaks a hold whose records show a session off Opus, and model-check-hold.sh set refuses the hold while one is; CLAUDE_MODEL_CHECK_OFF=1 turns it off), the Stop hook that makes every final reply open and close with its stamp and the ticket it works on (`· ticket: #N` or `ticket: none`, since 1.13.0) and rest any claim of who built a file, or how production stands, on something read that turn (since 1.15.0 a held reply is answered by one short line, never sent again), the PreToolUse gate that refuses a tool call whose preceding line has no stamp, a stamp naming no ticket, or one ahead of the clock (a final reply's stamp must be within a minute of it) or a task list left on one step for 12 tool calls (and, since 1.14.0, appends each passing call's `<epoch> <session> <tickets>` to the local activity log TICKET_ACTIVITY_LOG, ~/.claude/ticket-activity.log, with the Stop hook's `stop` line, so a project can count working time per ticket off the prompt; since 1.21.0, SMADPickleBot #1164, a call of Agent or Workflow writes `<epoch> <session> <tickets> delegated <tool_use_id>` and a subagent's own calls `<epoch> <session> agent <agent_id> <tool_use_id|->`, the parent call's id read from the agent's meta file when the Agent tool spawned it and `-` for a Workflow's agents, whose meta has none, so a ticket built by delegates counts their time too), the guard that refuses a long runner in the foreground and a PowerShell call that would strip the double quotes inside a native program's argument, and session-start checks for unpushed commits (its 10-minute rescan a detached job since 1.12.0, so a prompt pays stats and reads only), a stale install and (on Gene's Windows box) launches that would pop up a console window; and since 1.22.0 the session nanny (hooks/nanny.py, SMADPickleBot #1214), on PostToolUse and Stop: a background Bash run recorded from its start's result, and one that prints a wait, prints nothing for its first 30 s or stops growing for 120 s put in front of the session once at its next tool result, holding the turn's Stop once while it runs unexplained (NANNY_QUIET names commands quiet by design); since 1.22.1 the start is read from the result's fields (its task id, the output found under the temp folder's claude/<project>/<session>/tasks/), since the hook's event never carries the sentence the session is shown, and a start it cannot read keeps its shape as `unmatched` in the session's state; since 1.22.2 (SMADPickleBot #1277) a run piped through tail or redirected to a file, which writes its output only at its end, is quiet by design too; and since 1.23.0 (SMADPickleBot #1279) the comment gate (hooks/comment-sign.py, from the stamp gate on a Bash or PowerShell call naming a write's verb, a subagent's too): a GitHub comment a session writes with the owner's token, by gh issue/pr comment, a close's --comment, a review's body or gh api to a comments path, carries the signature line `— **<session>** · Claude session` (its text in the command, or ending a body file it names), the session's name from Claude Code's session registry, or the call is refused with the line to add; the gate never parses the shell, so no quoting refuses a signed comment; and since 1.27.0 (SMADPickleBot #1664) the one line the release-words recorder prints for a ship word (`record plain`) rides the clock's prompt context, where its output was discarded before; and since 1.28.0 (SMADPickleBot #1665) the model check keeps Opus until the weekly reset when every recorded session is on it with no hold on file (it sets the hold instead of reading the target fresh), and on the first prompt after a compaction or resume a session is told which re-stated skills are older than the newest installed copy (stale-skills.py, marked by plugin-version.sh at SessionStart), and on its first prompt after the desktop app's signed-in account changed it is handed the box's switch note (session-fresh.lib.sh; ACCOUNT_SWITCH_NOTE, default ~/.claude/account-switch-note.txt), so a hibernating session woken after a switch needs no pasted line; and since 1.29.0 (SMADPickleBot #1762) a box that keeps ~/.claude/model-check-sessions, one session title a line, has the model check read, switch and hold on those sessions alone, every other session left on its model; and since 1.30.0 (SMADPickleBot #1802) the Stop hook holds once a final reply that promises work starting now ("now I'll start #N", "moving on to #N", "next I start ...") with no condition in its sentence (when, once, after, until, if, your word, waits), so a session that says it is starting the next ticket starts it in that turn or says what it waits on (hooks/promise-gate.py); since 1.30.1 a stamp or evidence hold carries that promise in its reason, since those holds are answered by one short line that would end the turn; since 1.30.2 "that's my next step", "my next step is" and "I'm going to" count as promises too; since 1.30.3 quoted words never do; and since 1.31.0 (SMADPickleBot #1807) a tool result's clock is the time alone, unpushed-commits speaks on a prompt only when a repo, branch or owner joins or leaves its list (in a one-line form), and nanny answers in bash, before any Python, when the call starts no background run and the session has none recorded; and since 1.31.1 (SMADPickleBot #1815) the promise gate knows file, send, run, ship, open and make, and a promise that begins "and will ..."; and since 1.32.0 (SMADPickleBot #1816) a reply the regex lets go whose closing words carry a candidate word is read by Haiku (one headless turn, no tools or settings, 20 s bound, the Stop hook's limit 30 s), its PROMISE held once unless the sentence names what it waits on, any failure letting the reply go (PROMISE_JUDGE_OFF=1 turns it off); and since 1.32.1 (SMADPickleBot #1826) Haiku's 'PROMISE: NONE' is no promise, and the sentence it names must be a run of the reply's own words; and since 1.33.0 (SMADPickleBot #1827; Gene, 11/18/26 11:04 AM PT: "get rid of all empty-promise hooks with haiku") the promise gate is gone whole, the regex, the Haiku judge and the promise carried in the stamp and evidence holds, the Stop hook's limit back to 5 s: a project mails the session its next ticket after a push instead, a letter that starts the session's next turn; and since 1.34.0 (SMADPickleBot #1810; Gene, 11/18/26 4:20 AM PT: the hooks came "from 3 different places ... other sessions may not have all of them") the first two hooks a box used to wire by hand are the plugin's, so every box has them: no-shell-writes (PreToolUse on Bash and PowerShell: authored text never goes into a file through the shell) and reminder-gate (Stop: a reply that points at pending items lists them), each standing down while the box's own settings still name its copy (hooks/moved.lib.sh), so neither runs twice during the move; and since 1.35.0 two more: catch-up (on a prompt and at a session's start, at most once every 120 s, a checkout another session pushed under is fast-forwarded when that cannot lose work and the session told what moved, or told why it was not; CLAUDE_NO_CATCH_UP turns it off) and the commit rules (block-git-commits, PreToolUse on Bash: git add -A or ., commit -a, --no-verify, a force push without a lease and a commit not authored as Claude are refused, the last now also in the form `git -c ... commit -a`; the project's .claude/hooks/.disabled or CLAUDE_GIT_GUARD_OFF=1 turns it off), the second standing down while a project's own settings still wire its copy (moved_in_project); and since 1.36.0 catch-up is the whole freshness hook (repo-fresh.sh, one project's fetch-origin.sh until then; catch-up-hook.sh stays as its shim): the fetch in a detached job once a cache exists, the catch-up, how far behind the upstream and the default branch a checkout that could not move is, a CLAUDE.md that changed, the repos beside the project caught up with a rebase, and the session channel's doorbell for a project with a sibling <Project>-sessions repo (a missing clone said only when CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR or `sessions = true` in the project's .claude/gene-hooks.toml says it keeps one); it stands down while the project's settings wire fetch-origin.sh or the box's wire catch-up-hook.sh; the project's .claude/hooks/.disabled or CLAUDE_ORIGIN_HOOK_OFF=1 turns it off; and since 1.37.0 (SMADPickleBot #1917; Gene, 11/19/26 3:08 PM PT, on a session that read its next ticket and ended its turn: "But then proceed to do nothing!") the Stop hook holds a turn once when the session's project handed it a ticket to do now (a record at ~/.claude/do-now/<session id>.json, {ticket, at}, left by the project's own tool) and the ticket-activity log shows no tool call on that ticket since (hooks/do-now-gate.py, inside stamp-reply.py): it checks an action in the log, never the reply's words, so the promise gate stays gone; and since 1.41.0 (SMADPickleBot #2066; Gene, 11/20/26 1:25 PM PT, after a session sat idle 7.9 of 13.4 hours with over 40 cards queued, every stretch beginning at its own end of turn) that record holds up to three times where it held once, and with no record a project that keeps a `.do-now.json` at its root, {"next": [command ...]}, is asked at every end of turn for the session's next card (the command gets `--session-id`, 2.5 s at most, one JSON line {ticket, title, how} or {}): a card named holds the turn, and holds again at the next end of turn when the session made a tool call since, even in a turn already continuing from a Stop hook; a hold answered with no tool call is let go, the bound that keeps a session from being trapped.
